newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND CALL ON HOLLIOAKES, LOSE GOUGH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND CALL ON HOLLIOAKES, LOSE GOUGH.

text.p: England are counting on a breath of antipodean air to provide them with an essential shot in the arm in the fifth test against Australia starting on Thursday.

The Hollioake brothers, both from Melbourne but both strongly and devotedly English, have been called in to rescue the struggling home side who must win the final two tests to prevent Australia retaining the Ashes.

They will also have to help England overcome the loss on Wednesday of main strike bowler Darren Gough, who sent down only a few deliveries in the nets before conceding that an injured knee would not stand up to the rigours of a match essential to England.

Captain Michael Atherton said: "It's certainly a blow but we just have to get on with it. We've given ourselves plenty of options and I'm not too concerned, because Devon Malcolm and Andy Caddick, the bowlers who've come in, have proved they can win tests."

It is to the Hollioake boys that England look to help secure the victory they need at Trent Bridge to stop Australia, 2-1 up with two matches to play, from keeping the Ashes they have held since 1989.

The two brothers both seem certain to start. Adam, the Surrey captain, and 19-year-old Ben starred in the one-day international series earlier in the season, when England achieved what has since turned out to have been a misleading 3-0 whitewash.

That success carried the side to a first test triumph at Edgbaston, even without the Hollioakes, who have been summoned after demoralising drubbings in the third and fourth matches of the six-test series.
England were beaten by 268 runs at Old Trafford and by an innings and 61 runs at Headingley, only once passing 200 runs in four innings.

Though doubts exist about the true test-match quality of the brothers, they do have the undimmed enthusiasm of youngsters yet to suffer the sort of defeats handed out to their seniors over the past six weeks.
Ben Hollioake's vibrant 98 in the recent Benson and Hedges Cup final at Lord's to follow his 63 there in the one-day international confirmed that he does not lack big-match temperament either.

Atherton warned against expecting too much of the teenager, who will become England's youngest player for almost 50 years unless the state of the Trent Bridge pitch tempts the selectors to pick two spinners in Robert Croft and Phil Tufnell.
"This is another big step up for him and people shouldn't expect miracles," the captain warned. "I'm sure in time he'll become an England regular, but it takes time to settle in."
The Antipodean connection does not stop there for Caddick was born and bred in New Zealand.
He was dropped for the fourth test after helping to win the first by taking five for 50 as the under-prepared Australians were shot out for 118 at Edgbaston.
Since then Gough has become England's leading wicket-taker and in his absence Malcolm, who had been placed on stand-by, looks even more certain to play.
Atherton added: "We made one or two changes because we felt things were flagging a bit. Now it's a matter of having the collective self-belief to make the most of the opportunities that come around.

"Even though we did lose the last two tests, we did have chances in both of them, but didn't take full advantage. This is a big game for us, because if we can win, we would go to The Oval as favourites. We've got a good record there and would really fancy our chances of winning the Ashes."
With heavy rain forecast, England, as usual, will keep their options open until the morning of the match on a pitch traditionally favourable to batsmen.
Australian skipper Mark Taylor will lead an unchanged team full of confidence after resounding victories in the previous two tests.
"We've played the better cricket over the past month and if we perform to our capabilities we can put any side under pressure," he said.
"We had problems at the start of the tour but the guys responded well. They worked damn hard and came storming back. There's still a job to be done and we want to finish it off in style."

Teams: England (from)- Michael Atherton (captain), Alec Stewart, John Crawley, Nasser Hussain, Graham Thorpe, Adam Hollioake, Ben Hollioake, Robert Croft, Andy Caddick, Dean Headley, Devon Malcolm, Phil Tufnell.
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Elliott, Greg Blewett, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Ricky Ponting, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Jason Gillespie, Glenn McGrath.
